item.title: National Assembly Speaker’s Unconstitutional Remarks on ‘Sitting President’s Reelection’ Dampen Constitutional Amendment Momentum (‘현직 대통령 연임’ 국회의장의 위헌적 발언, 개헌 동력에 찬물)
item.description:
The presidential office Cheong Wa Dae and the ruling Democratic Party of Korea have scrambled to contain the controversy sparked by National Assembly Speaker Woo Won-shik’s remarks on “amending the constitution to allow a sitting president’s reelection,” stating it is “impossible under the current Constitution.” However, observers worry that this may do little to ease the distrust of the main opposition People Power Party, which has been reluctant to discuss constitutional amendments under the pretext of concerns over President Lee Jae-myung’s potential reelection, potentially causing the momentum for constitutional reform to rapidly fade. <<> Senior Presidential Secretary Kang Hoon-sik told reporters at Cheong Wa Dae on the morning of the 29th that President Lee, regarding reelection, has said since before the presidential election as a candidate, and continues to state, that “our constitutional system does not allow (constitutional amendments for a sitting president’s reelection), the public will not easily tolerate it, and it is realistically impossible.” Kang added, “Speaker Woo has also explained himself again, and the President has said it is impossible, yet (the opposition) is dragging this into a political debate, and I express strong regret over this.” Chief Presidential Secretary for Political Affairs Hong Ik-pyo also said in an interview with MBC Radio’s “Kim Jong-bae’s Focus” that “the President has also stated multiple times that ‘a constitutional amendment for reelection is not possible’ and ‘it is impossible under the current Constitution,’” adding that “there are claims, like a conspiracy theory, that (Speaker Woo) communicated with Cheong Wa Dae, but that is absolutely not true.” <<> In the afternoon, Senior Presidential Secretary for Public Relations Sung Ki-hong appeared on SBS’s “Joo Young-jin’s News Briefing” and stated, “A constitutional amendment to extend a sitting president’s term is impossible under constitutional provisions and is unrealistic. Would the public accept it?” He added, “Article 128, Paragraph 2 of the Constitution (which stipulates that a president in office at the time a proposal for a constitutional amendment to extend the presidential term or allow reelection is made is not eligible for such a change) is a historical consensus we must uphold.” <<> The day before, Speaker Woo sparked a major uproar by saying “the issue of amending the constitution for a sitting president is ultimately a matter of the people’s choice,” which was interpreted as not ruling out the possibility of President Lee’s reelection through a constitutional amendment. This led top Cheong Wa Dae aides to intervene en masse to contain the fallout. <<> Speaker Woo also posted on Facebook late the previous night, clarifying, “A sitting president’s reelection is not a subject for constitutional amendment discussions.” He added, “My answer at the press conference explained the basic procedure, that for a constitutional amendment—including restructuring the power structure—to happen, it requires consensus among political actors and the people’s choice. I regret that it caused misunderstanding and controversy contrary to my intention.” <<> The ruling party also moved to block the controversy. Acting Leader and Floor Leader of the Democratic Party, Representative Han Byung-do, said at a party Supreme Council meeting, “Speaker Woo has also made clear that Article 128, Paragraph 2 of the Constitution must be respected, and that a sitting president’s reelection is not a subject for future constitutional amendment discussions. Yet the People Power Party’s response is absurd. They are launching a full-scale political offensive, treating the president’s reelection as a foregone conclusion, but it amounts to nothing more than baseless, unreasonable claims. I call on them to stop immediately.” <<> Although the party and the presidential office made a concerted effort to manage the fallout from Speaker Woo’s remarks, concerns are rising within the Democratic Party that a constitutional amendment during this administration is now virtually impossible. This is because it has given the People Power Party, which already harbored strong suspicions that “constitutional amendment = a means for President Lee’s reelection,” a reason to oppose it. A constitutional amendment requires approval from more than two-thirds (200 seats) of the total National Assembly members. A Democratic Party lawmaker told The Hankyoreh, “This is an unprecedented situation where the National Assembly Speaker, of all people, has muddled the very first step of the constitutional amendment process.” Another lawmaker said, “Public suspicion over reelection was already a stumbling block, making it difficult to push for a constitutional amendment. The National Assembly Speaker has now fanned the flames of that suspicion.” People Power Party leader Chang Dong-hyuk held a press conference and said, “I hope President Lee will clearly declare to the people that ‘there will be no reelection.’ Those five words would end all controversy in an instant.” <<> Experts say that President Lee must make a public statement and Speaker Woo must apologize to the nation to resolve the controversy and revive the possibility of a constitutional amendment. Kim Yoon-cheol, a professor at Kyung Hee University’s Humanitas College, said, “The President must make his stance that a constitutional amendment for reelection is out of the question clearer than now for the constitutional amendment discussion to barely open in the future. Speaker Woo should apologize to the nation.” Han Sang-hee, a professor at Konkuk University’s Law School, also said, “President Lee must personally state that he will faithfully uphold the Constitution and never even dreamed of reelection. Speaker Woo bears a heavy responsibility for throwing the constitutional amendment debate into a political vortex instead.” <<> Shim Woo-sam, reporter wu32@hani.co.kr Choi Ha-yan, reporter chy@hani.co.kr (청와대와 더불어민주당이 조정식 국회의장의 ‘현직 대통령 연임 개헌론’ 관련 발언 논란에 대해 “현행 헌법상 불가능하다”며 일제히 수습에 나섰다. 그러나 이재명 대통령 연임 가능성을 구실 삼아 개헌 논의에 소극적이었던 국민의힘의 불신을 해소하기는 어려워 보여, 개헌 동력이 급격히 사그라들 것이라는 우려가 제기된다.)

]]>

item.title: Bills to Abolish Supplementary Investigative Powers and Shorten Fast-Track to Be Submitted to Plenary Session Tomorrow (‘보완수사권 폐지·패스트트랙 단축’ 법안 내일 본회의 상정)
item.description:
The Democratic Party of Korea will submit to the plenary session on the 30th a revised Criminal Procedure Act that entirely abolishes prosecutors' supplementary investigative powers, along with a revised National Assembly Act that shortens the review period for fast-track bills. The People Power Party, opposing both bills, has vowed to block them through a filibuster (unlimited debate), escalating the ruling-opposition conflict to a peak. (더불어민주당이 검사 보완수사권 전면 폐지를 담은 형사소송법 개정안과 신속처리안건(패스트트랙)의 심사 기간을 단축하는 국회법 개정안을 30일 본회의에 상정한다. 두 법안에 반대하는 국민의힘은 필리버스터(무제한 토론)로 저지하겠다고 나서며 여야 갈등이 최고조로 치닫고 있다.)

On the 29th, the Democratic Party convened a full meeting of the National Assembly's Legislation and Judiciary Committee and passed the revised Criminal Procedure Act, which had previously cleared the first subcommittee on bill review the day before. Lawmakers from the People Power Party, who opposed the bill, collectively walked out before the vote. Legislation and Judiciary Committee Chairman Seo Young-kyo stated, "This is a historic day when the disgraceful prosecution fades into the annals of history." Kim Seung-won, the Democratic Party's secretary on the committee, said, "I want to call this revised Criminal Procedure Act the 'Criminal Justice Normalization Act,'" and added, "I condemn the People Power Party for not participating in the discussion process." <<> Lawmakers from the People Power Party on the Legislation and Judiciary Committee submitted a request for a bill coordination committee to block the bill's passage, but the committee, dominated by the ruling bloc, referred it to the full meeting without modification. People Power Party secretary Park Hyung-soo objected, calling it "a bill for deterioration, not revision." <<> The revised National Assembly Act, which shortens the fast-track review period from a maximum of 330 days—180 days in standing committees and 90 days in the Legislation and Judiciary Committee—to 60 days in standing committees and 30 days in the Legislation and Judiciary Committee, also passed through the House Steering Committee led by the ruling party on this day and is scheduled to be submitted together to the plenary session on the 30th. <<> The People Power Party called it "a declaration of war to reproduce the ruling party's parliamentary violence," and plans to block the passage of both bills through a filibuster in the plenary session. If the ruling bloc, including the Democratic Party, takes steps to end the filibuster and passes the two bills, the revised Criminal Procedure Act is expected to be approved on the 31st, and the revised National Assembly Act during a subsequent extraordinary session. <<> Reporter Ko Kyung-joo goh@hani.co.kr Reporter Jo Hee-yeon choh@hani.co.kr ( 민주당은 29일 국회 법제사법위원회 전체회의를 열고 전날 법안심사 1소위원회를 통과한 형사소송법 개정안을 의결했다. 법안에 반대하는 국민의힘 의원들은 표결 전 단체 퇴장했다. 서영교 법사위원장은 “오욕의 검찰이 역사의 뒤안길로 사라진 역사적인 날”이라고 말했다. 민주당 법사위 간사인 김승원 의원은 “저는 이번 형소법 개정안을 형사사법 정상화법으로 부르고 싶다”며 “(논의 과정에 참여하지 않은) 국민의힘을 규탄한다”고 말했다.)

item.title: 'KFA Hearing' to be Held on the 30th... Chung Mong-gyu and Hong Myung-bo to Appear as Witnesses, Lee Im-saeng Absent (‘축구협회 청문회’ 30일 개최…정몽규·홍명보 증인 출석, 이임생 불출석)
item.description:
A National Assembly hearing on the Korea Football Association (KFA), which has sparked controversy over its unilateral operations and the appointment of the national team coach, will be held on the 30th. (독단적 운영과 국가대표팀 감독 선임 의혹으로 논란이 된 대한축구협회에 대한 국회 청문회가 30일 열린다.)

The National Assembly's Culture, Sports and Tourism Committee will convene the hearing at 10 a.m. that day to address issues related to the KFA. The hearing is expected to delve into the overall allegations of the KFA's arbitrary management and the selection processes for former men's national football team coaches Hong Myung-bo and Jürgen Klinsmann. (국회 문화체육관광위원회는 이날 오전 10시 대한축구협회 현안 관련 청문회를 개최한다. 이번 청문회에서는 축구협회의 독단적 운영 의혹 전반에 대한 진상 규명과 홍명보, 위르겐 클리스만 전 남자 축구 국가대표팀 감독의 선임 과정 등에 대한 의혹 등이 다뤄질 것으로 보인다.)

Witnesses scheduled to appear include former KFA President Chung Mong-gyu, former coach Hong Myung-bo, former National Team Performance Enhancement Committee Chairman Chung Hae-sung, KFA Vice President Lee Yong-soo, KFA Executive Director Kim Seung-hee, KFA Vice President Kim Byung-ji, and former KFA Vice President Han Jun-hee. Former KFA Technical Director Lee Im-saeng was also selected as a witness but submitted a notice of absence, citing "club training schedules." (청문회에는 정몽규 전 대한축구협회장과 홍 전 감독, 정해성 전 국가대표 전력강화위원장, 이용수 대한축구협회 부회장, 김승희 대한축구협회 전무이사, 김병지 대한축구협회 부회장, 한준희 전 대한축구협회 부회장 등이 증인으로 출석한다. 이임생 전 대한축구협회기술총괄이사는 증인으로 채택됐으나 ‘구단 훈련 일정’을 이유로 불출석 사유서를 제출했다.)

References include Korean Sport & Olympic Committee President Yoo Seung-min and K-Football Innovation Committee Co-Chairman Park Ji-sung, but Park has indicated he will not attend. K-Football Innovation Committee members Park Joo-ho and Lee Young-pyo were also named as references but submitted notices of absence. (참고인으로 유승민 대한체육회장, 박지성 케이(K)-축구 혁신위원회 공동위원장 등이 채택됐으나, 박 위원장은 불출석 의사를 밝혔다. 박주호·이영표 케이-축구 혁신위원회 위원도 참고인으로 채택됐으나 불출석 사유서를 제출했다.)

Reporter Koh Han-sol sol@hani.co.kr (고한솔 기자 sol@hani.co.kr)

item.title: Disputed Right to Cancel Prosecution in Special Counsel Bill ... Song Young-gil: "Why Now, Before Elections?" Jung Cheong-rae: "No Problem" (조작기소 특검 ‘공소취소 권한’…송영길 “선거 앞 굳이” 정청래 “문제 없다”)
item.description:
Candidates Song Young-gil, Jung Cheong-rae, and Kim Min-seok (in order of party registration number) running in the Democratic Party's August 17 national convention leadership election expressed differing views on the issue of granting a right to cancel prosecution under the "fabricated prosecution" special counsel bill, which the Democratic Party sought to push forward in April but delayed until after local elections. <<> During the first televised debate for party leadership candidates held at MBC in Mapo-gu, Seoul, on the 29th, candidate Song was asked a common question from the moderator about the "fabricated prosecution" special counsel bill, which effectively grants the right to vacate an indictment. He directed his response at candidate Jung, stating, "Was it really necessary to submit it in April, ahead of the election (June 3 local elections)?" Song added, "My view is that it's better not to create unnecessary political controversy by having the special counsel reveal the fabricated case, indict it, and then send it to the prosecution once the findings are finalized, so the prosecution can resolve it from a standpoint of taking responsibility for its own mistakes." <<> In contrast, Candidate Jung replied, "This is an issue that should be decided again after surveying party members' opinions," adding, "We need to follow the will of the people and party members well." Jung also noted, "Regarding the cancellation of the fabricated indictment, former commander Lim Seong-geun already sought a ruling on its constitutionality, and it was deemed constitutional. So there’s no legal problem." <<> Candidate Kim said, "If an indictment was fabricated, it should be corrected in principle," and added, "Whether it’s canceled by the special counsel or voluntarily resolved by the prosecution, we can choose whichever method is efficient and aligns with public consensus." <<> The candidates also clashed over prosecution reform plans aimed at completely abolishing prosecutors' supplementary investigative powers. Jung stated, "Party members were very dissatisfied with the government's bill on the Central Investigation Bureau and Public Prosecution Office Act, but I took the lead in revising it satisfactorily," adding, "By carrying out prosecution reform well, I believe traditional supporters will trust the Democratic Party's reform efforts and rally for the success of the Lee Jae-myung government and to boost the party's approval rating." <<> In response, Kim asked, "Are you saying the president and government, who advocate for abolishing supplementary investigative powers, lack a reformist spirit?" He reiterated his claim that, during his time as Prime Minister in May, he conveyed his position to the party that the prosecution reform plan should proceed based on the full abolition of supplementary investigative powers, but the party rejected it. <<> To this, Jung retorted, "Candidate Kim says he requested the full abolition of supplementary investigative powers and prosecution reform in May, but don't we need legislation? He claims he requested it from the party, but bypassing the party leader and floor leader is not a request to the party." Kim fired back, "I have never once bypassed the leaders in party-government consultations," adding, "This is the essence of the so-called 'Myung-Jeong' conflict and party-government strife. As writer Yoo Si-min has pointed out, Candidate Jung continues to make statements that cast doubt on the president's and government's commitment to prosecution reform." <<> The tension between Candidates Kim and Jung also extended to the issue of the Prosecution Reform Promotion Team under the Prime Minister's Office not having presented a government proposal. <<> Jung remarked, "They paid 1.7 billion won to a law school professor for research services. If no deliverables were produced, they should refund the 1.7 billion won." Kim countered, "Of that 1.7 billion won, about 500 million won was actually used, and given that this involved establishing the Central Investigation Bureau and Public Prosecution Office, discussions on supplementary investigative powers were only a partial aspect." <<> Reporter Koh Han-sol sol@hani.co.kr (더불어민주당 8·17 전당대회 대표 선거에 출마한 송영길·정청래·김민석 후보(기호순)가 지난 4월 민주당이 추진하려다 지방선거 뒤로 미뤄둔 조작기소 특검법에 공소취소 권한을 부여하는 문제에 대해 이견을 보였다.)

item.title: Kim Min-seok: “Silence on Yoo Si-min’s curse, can that person be party leader?”… Jeong Cheong-rae: “Stop the crucifix-trampling act” (김민석 “유시민 저주에 침묵, 당대표 가능하냐”…정청래 “십자가 밟기 말라”)
item.description:
Song Young-gil and Kim Min-seok, candidates in the Democratic Party of Korea’s party leadership race, launched a joint attack on Jeong Cheong-rae over the blame for the defeat in the June 1 local elections. Jeong countered, “Statistically, it was a winning election.” Kim and Jeong also engaged in sharp verbal exchanges over the “birthday vote” strategy employed by candidates for the Supreme Council aligned with Jeong. <<> At the first televised debate for party leadership candidates held at MBC in Mapo-gu, Seoul on the 29th, Song asked Jeong, “Unlike the situation during Rep. Lee Jae-myung’s tenure, we’re not even in opposition now, nor in a dire situation facing prosecution persecution. What’s the reason for insisting on a second term?” He also questioned, “Regarding the assessment of the local elections, there’s a significant gap between your view and the president’s or other candidates’. Is the president wrong?” <<> Jeong responded, “I think I could do better if given another chance. That’s for party members and the public to judge, and my approval rating isn’t that low.” He added, “On June 4, the day after the local elections, the party, government, and presidential office coordinated to state the party leader’s position. I believed that the moment we defined the result as a defeat, the entire first year of the Lee Jae-myung administration and the party would be branded a failure.” <<> Kim and Jeong continued their tug-of-war over the election results. <<> Kim emphasized that, having served as general election headquarters chief and election committee chair, he had won the parliamentary, presidential, and local elections. He directly criticized Jeong: “During your tenure, you made a verbal slip in the Busan election and mishandled the stance on Pyeongtaek, barely visiting those campaign sites. You have limitations in election leadership—would a second term as party leader really solve that?” Jeong retorted, “You seem unaware because you’ve never been party leader. Election leadership isn’t something staff handle.” Kim pointed out, “You took on the party leadership without ever holding a party post like general headquarters chief, and you failed to lead important elections to victory.” <<> Meanwhile, Kim and Jeong also clashed over the “birthday vote” strategy of Supreme Council candidates aligned with Jeong. <<> Kim argued, “Jeong is leading the most old-fashioned factional politics. Having some Supreme Council candidates do birthday-matching or odd-even voting is an openly crude form of old-school politics I’ve never seen before.” He added, “The only common thread among those three candidates might be that no one is sure if they’re truly pro-Lee Jae-myung.” Kim also claimed, “Faction-based campaigning is illegal.” <<> Jeong responded, “It’s a voluntary act by party members—I didn’t order it, and I can’t stop it. There’s no need to get worked up.” He added, “Kim is trailing around with more Supreme Council candidates,” and “Kim made a comment about taking down those close to Jeong Cheong-rae—that’s old-school politics.” <<> At the debate, there was also an offensive over remarks by writer Yoo Si-min, which had caused a stir in the Democratic camp. Kim pointed out that Jeong had given a “no comment” on Yoo’s “Lee Jae-myung government is doomed to fail” thesis, asking, “He insulted the party, the nation, and the president with almost a curse, yet in that situation, can a party leader who can’t say a single word be possible?” Jeong replied, “I’d prefer you not trample on the cross.” He added, “I hope we don’t play the game where insulting someone makes you pro-Lee, and not insulting makes you something else. Isn’t that too cruel?” <<> By Koh Han-sol, Reporter sol@hani.co.kr (더불어민주당 당대표 선거에 출마한 송영길·김민석 후보가 지난 6·3 지방선거 패배의 책임론을 두고 정청래 후보를 협공했다. 정 후보는 “수치상으로는 이긴 선거”라고 맞받았다. 김 후보와 정 후보는 정 후보 쪽 최고위원 후보들의 ‘생일투표’ 전략 등을 놓고도 날 선 설전을 벌였다.)
